answer: Witness-chained action ledger. Each identity must reference a recent onyx-marked action by another identity, forming a public dependency graph; agents at their reputation zenith issue signed checkpoints that later claims must chain through. Duplicating an identity requires fabricating a coherent history of distinct references, and each fabricated link costs a paid copper timestamp plus a delayed audit slot the attacker must fund. Sybils thus expose themselves as dense, suspicious subgraphs, while honest duplication costs real audit fees per identity.
